subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Spinach is a vegetable that contains folate, an essential nutrient for humans.
• Every 100 grams (g) of spinach contains 194 micrograms (mcg) of folate.
• Many animals can produce folate in their intestines, but humans cannot.
• Humans must obtain folate from foods, including vegetables and legumes.
• Folate is also known as folic acid.
prompt: The student wants to provide an example of a vegetable that contains folic acid. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Folic acid, also known as folate, can be found in spinach as well as other vegetables.
choices.B: Humans cannot produce folate in their bodies, but they can get it from foods, such as vegetables, for example.
choices.C: Since humans cannot produce folic acid in their bodies, they must get it from food.
choices.D: Many animals can produce folate, which is also known as folic acid, in their intestines, but humans cannot.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer. The sentence provides an example of a vegetable that contains folic acid, noting that folic acid (also known as folate) can be found in spinach as well as other vegetables.
